about.title: Rancho Cordova Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product does not have to be exotic to hurt someone. In Rancho Cordova, it might be a space heater in an apartment off Zinfandel Drive, a power tool picked up along Sunrise Boulevard, a child's car seat, or a tire that gives out on Folsom Boulevard. Sacramento County's public records logged 292 injury collisions and 426 people injured in the city during 2025, and some crashes anywhere raise the question of whether an airbag, seat belt, or brake component performed the way it was built to. California treats these cases differently from an ordinary negligence claim. Under strict liability, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You show the item had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect, and that the defect caused your injury. The focus lands on the product itself, so keeping the item, its packaging, and any receipts matters. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Rancho Cordova residents with an independent attorney who handles defective-product claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Rancho Cordova Residents Use LawProactive for Defective-Product Claims

items.title: Strict liability, not a negligence fight
items.desc: California law often lets an injured person recover by showing the product was defective and caused harm, without proving the company was careless. The attorney we connect you with builds the claim around that standard from the start.

items.title: Preserving the product is step one
items.desc: The item itself is usually the central evidence, so we encourage you to keep it, its packaging, and any instructions exactly as they are. An independent attorney can then arrange proper storage and testing.

items.title: Everyone in the chain can be answerable
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the retailer where you bought the product may each be responsible under California law. That matters when a maker is overseas or hard to identify.

items.question: I bought the product at a store in Rancho Cordova, but it was made overseas. Who can I make a claim against?
items.answer: California allows claims against more than just the manufacturer. The distributor and the local retailer that sold you the product, whether on Sunrise Boulevard or anywhere else in Sacramento County, may also be strictly liable. An independent attorney can sort out which parties in that chain are realistic to pursue.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company was negligent?
items.answer: Usually not. In a California strict product liability claim, you generally need to show the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. How careful the company was is often not the central question.

items.question: I already threw away the broken product. Is my claim over?
items.answer: Not necessarily, though it does make things harder, so stop discarding anything else related to it now. Photos, receipts, packaging, medical records, and the same model purchased elsewhere can still help establish a defect. Talk with an attorney about what evidence remains before assuming there is no path forward.
